    Fischbacher §5.4: the end case of Case B #

    The last kept bound e of the chain lies above the right peak d of the replaced segment. Then the new peak e is joined to the later old peaks one at a time: while the next old peak lies below e, its segment is dropped, and a one-segment cycle avoiding c moves the separation at e along (Lemma 4.4); at the last old peak the end of the walk is rebuilt along w as for the initial walk. Separation at e starts from Lemma 4.3 for the last link.

    (∃ (R₀ : List (ZSeg A)), L₂ = R₀ ++ R ∧ ZLast σ.d R₀ = Q) → ∀ (p : Quiver.Path (RayVert.mk Q) (RayVert.mk e)), 0 < p.length → (∀ (x₂ : RayVert A) (p₀ : Quiver.Path (RayVert.mk Q) x₂) (e₂ : x₂ ⟶ RayVert.mk e), p = p₀.cons e₂ → ¬SepComp (z.hull \ {σ.c}) e ⟨x₁.out, ↑e₁⟩ ⟨x₂.out, ↑e₂⟩) → ∃ (z' : ZWalk b), z'.d₀ = z.d₀ ∧ z'.Good w ∧ z'.hull ⊂ z.hull

    Joining the new peak e to the later old peaks. Starting from a path p from an old peak Q (with the old segments R after it) up to e, whose last arrow is separated from the left arrow e₁ at e, the end of the walk is rebuilt (hfinish).
